sections.name: When Heroin Was Cough Medicine
lines: In 1898, a German company started selling a brand new cough medicine. It was called Heroin.
Bayer named it heroin, from the German word for heroic, because it was meant to be so powerful.
It really did calm coughs, at a time when diseases like tuberculosis were common.
It was even sold as a safer, less addictive alternative to morphine.
Within a few years, doctors noticed patients becoming badly addicted.
In the US, heroin was banned completely in 1924. Bayer's other new drug from that time did better. Aspirin.
